    한국어

Litpage is an open-source workspace you run yourself. Write in a block editor, organize pages and teams, track work in
databases with a dozen views, share with fine-grained permissions, and bring your own AI key for chat, agents and
writing help. The whole app is one Node.js process with one SQLite file, small enough for a laptop or a single
server.

> **Try the demo:** open [litpage-demo-production.up.railway.app](https://litpage-demo-production.up.railway.app) and click **Try the demo**, no sign-up.
> You get your own workspace with sample pages, nobody else can see it, and it is deleted after 4 hours. AI is not
> connected in the demo.

## Why Litpage

- **Self-hosted and small.** One process, one SQLite database (`node:sqlite` with full-text search), your files in one
  folder. No Postgres, Redis or queue to run.
- **Docs and data together.** Pages, a block editor and databases live in the same tree, so a project brief and its task
  board sit side by side.
- **Real collaboration.** Live multi-user editing over WebSocket, comments and suggested edits, version history, teams,
  page-level and field-level permissions, public sharing and published sites.
- **AI on your terms.** Chat, custom agents, AI blocks, autofill and meeting-note summaries run on the provider and key
  you configure. Without a key, everything else works.
- **Open to your tools.** A REST API with webhooks and an MCP endpoint for AI clients, with tokens you control.
- **Two languages.** The interface comes in English and Korean.

## Feature tour

        Block editor.  41 block types, slash menu, markdown shortcuts, drag and drop, mentions, comments and
      suggested edits.

        Databases.  Typed fields, filters, sorts, groups, formulas, relations, rollups, templates, buttons and
      automations.

        Many views of the same data.  Table, board, list, gallery, calendar, timeline, chart, dashboard, feed,
      form and map.

        Charts and dashboards.  Column, bar, line, donut and number charts straight from a database.

        AI that knows your workspace.  Ask about your pages, draft and edit text, fill database fields, and run
      custom agents on a schedule or trigger.

        English and Korean.  Switch the interface language in Settings.

  Everything that is included

- **Editor**: rich text, 41 block types, slash menu, markdown shortcuts, drag and drop, mentions, equations, code
  blocks with highlighting, embeds, comments and suggested edits, version history, real-time collaboration.
- **Workspace**: pages and sub-pages, sidebar with favorites and recents, teams, sharing and permissions, published
  sites, import (Markdown, CSV, HTML, Word, PDF) and export, inbox and notifications, reminders, trash, light and dark
  themes.
- **Databases**: table, board, list, gallery, calendar, timeline, chart, dashboard, feed, form and map views; filters,
  sorts, groups, formulas, relations, rollups, unique IDs, automations, buttons, templates, field-level access rules.
- **AI** (optional): chat with workspace search, custom agents with triggers and schedules, a writing assistant, AI
  blocks, database autofill, a formula assistant, meeting notes with summaries, image generation where the provider
  supports it.
- **Admin**: workspace settings, members and guests, security policies, audit log, analytics, passkeys and two-step
  verification.
- **Developers**: REST API with personal access tokens and integrations, webhooks, an MCP endpoint.

## Quick start

### With Docker

```bash
docker build -t litpage .
docker run -d --name litpage -p 3001:3001 -v litpage-data:/data \
  -e NC_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL=you@example.com -e NC_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD='change-me' \
  litpage
```

Open http://localhost:3001 and sign in with that email and password ("Continue with a password"). Data (the SQLite
database and uploaded files) lives in the `litpage-data` volume.

### From source

Requirements: Node.js 26 or later and pnpm 10 (`npm install -g pnpm@10.32.1`).

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev            # API on http://127.0.0.1:3001, web app on http://127.0.0.1:5173
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:5173 and enter any email address. In development mode the login code is shown on screen, and
onboarding creates your first workspace. Data lives in `apps/server/data/`.

For a production build served by the API server on port 3001:

```bash
pnpm build && pnpm start
```

## Configuration

Set these as environment variables (in development, `apps/server/.env.local` is read too; it is git-ignored).

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` / `HOST` | `3001` / `127.0.0.1` | Where the server listens (the Docker image uses `0.0.0.0`). |
| `NC_DATA_DIR` | `apps/server/data` | SQLite database and uploaded files. Mount a persistent volume here. |
| `NC_PUBLIC_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:5173` | Public address, used in links inside emails. |
| `NC_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL`, `NC_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` | unset | Creates the first account on a fresh production install. |
| `NC_DEMO_MODE` | unset | Set to `1` for a hardened public demo where every visitor gets a temporary workspace of their own. Account identity, workspace control, sharing, integrations, outbound actions and public exposure are blocked. |
| `NC_DEMO_SANDBOX_HOURS` | `4` | In demo mode, how long a visitor's workspace lives before it is deleted. |
| `NC_DEMO_MAX_SANDBOXES` | `300` | In demo mode, how many visitor workspaces may exist at once. When full, expired ones are deleted first, otherwise new visitors are asked to try again later. |
| `NC_DEMO_MAX_RECORDS` | `5000` | In demo mode, blocks, database rows, comments and other records per visitor workspace. |
| `NC_DEMO_MAX_UPLOAD_MB`, `NC_DEMO_MAX_FILES` | `25`, `50` | In demo mode, uploaded files per visitor workspace (each file is limited to 5 MB). |
| `NC_DEMO_SANDBOXES_PER_IP_HOUR`, `NC_DEMO_SANDBOXES_PER_IP_DAY` | `5`, `20` | In demo mode, new workspaces per client address (behind a proxy, set `NC_TRUST_PROXY=1`). |
| `NC_DEMO_RESET_HOURS` | unset | In demo mode, wipe the configured data directory before opening SQLite and exit cleanly after this many hours (a safety net; keep it longer than `NC_DEMO_SANDBOX_HOURS`). Use it only where the platform restarts a process that exits cleanly; Railway does not, so leave it unset there (visitor workspaces clean themselves up). |
| `NC_SMTP_URL`, `NC_MAIL_FROM` | unset | Outgoing mail (`smtp://` or `smtps://` URL). Without it, mail is only kept in the development outbox. |
| `NC_TRUST_PROXY` | unset | Set to `1` behind a reverse proxy so client addresses come from `X-Forwarded-*`. |
| `NC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | unset | Extra origins allowed to call the API, comma separated. |
| AI variables | unset | See [AI with your own key](#ai-with-your-own-key). |

### Demo mode

Set `NC_DEMO_MODE=1` to publish a public demo. The login page shows **Try the demo**: one click creates a temporary account and a workspace named “Litpage Demo” with a “Start here” page and sample pages (Roadmap, Projects, Meeting notes, Team wiki), and signs the visitor in. Each visitor only ever sees their own workspace, and it is deleted with everything in it (pages, comments, history, search entries, files) `NC_DEMO_SANDBOX_HOURS` after it was created; a background job checks every few minutes. “Start over” in the notice bar replaces it with a fresh one. Workspaces per client address, live workspaces, records and uploads are limited (see the table above).

The server refuses account identity, workspace administration, invitations, sharing and publishing, integrations and tokens, webhooks, public forms, AI and other outbound actions, and anything that would reach another visitor. If `NC_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL` and `NC_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` are set, the login page also keeps the email form so that shared account can sign in as before; without them the email form is hidden. `NC_DEMO_RESET_HOURS` additionally wipes the data directory on start and restarts the process periodically. Treat all demo data as disposable, and use it only where the platform restarts a process that exits cleanly (not on Railway).

## AI with your own key

All AI features go through one provider configured on the server. Keys stay on the server: they are never sent to the
browser and are masked in logs and errors.

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Uses an OpenAI Responses API compatible endpoint. |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | Optional, defaults to `https://api.openai.com/v1`. Point it at any compatible endpoint. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Uses the Anthropic API (optional `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`). |
| `NC_AI_MODEL`, `NC_AI_FAST_MODEL` | Default model, and a model for short tasks such as titles and autofill. |
| `NC_AI_PROVIDER` | `openai`, `anthropic` or `none`. When unset, OpenAI is used if `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set, otherwise Anthropic if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. |

`node scripts/tools/openai-smoke.mjs` sends a few short requests to check a live endpoint. Tests and end-to-end scripts
only talk to local mock servers.

## API and integrations

- **REST API** at `/v1` for pages, databases, data sources, blocks, comments, users and search. Create a personal access
  token or an integration in Settings, then:

  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3001/v1/search \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITPAGE_TOKEN" \
    -H "Litpage-Version: 2026-10-01" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"page_size": 10}'
  ```

  The `Litpage-Version` header is optional and defaults to the current version.
- **Webhooks** for page, database and comment events, signed with HMAC-SHA256 and retried on failure.
- **MCP endpoint** at `/api/mcp` so AI clients that speak the Model Context Protocol can search and edit the pages you
  can access, with the same permission checks as the app.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Browser
    UI["React 19 app editor, databases, AI panel"]
  end
  subgraph Server["One Node.js process"]
    RPC["JSON RPC /api/rpc"]
    WS["Real-time sync WebSocket"]
    REST["REST API and webhooks /v1"]
    MCP["MCP endpoint /api/mcp"]
    AI["AI service chat, agents, autofill"]
    DB[("SQLite with full-text search")]
    FILES[("Uploaded files")]
  end
  PROVIDER["Your AI provider OpenAI compatible or Anthropic"]
  TOOLS["Your scripts and tools"]
  CLIENTS["MCP clients"]
  UI --> RPC
  UI   WS
  RPC --> DB
  RPC --> FILES
  WS --> DB
  REST --> DB
  TOOLS --> REST
  CLIENTS --> MCP
  MCP --> AI
  RPC --> AI
  AI --> PROVIDER
```

```
packages/shared   records, operations, rich text, permissions, database query and formula engine
apps/server       Node 26 + Hono + node:sqlite + WebSocket
apps/web          React 19 + Vite
e2e               end-to-end scripts (Chrome via playwright-core)
docs              architecture.md, how-it-was-built.md
```

More in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Development

```bash
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test                                               # unit tests: shared, server, web
cd e2e && NC_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:5173 node smoke.mjs  # end-to-end, one script per area
```

The end-to-end scripts drive Google Chrome (default macOS path in `e2e/lib.mjs`) against a dev server. The images in
this README come from `scripts/readme/` (capture, then build the assets).

## How it was built

Litpage started as an experiment for a YouTube series: how far can AI coding agents get when they build a full
block-based workspace app? A lead Claude Code session split the work into areas and coordinated subagents, with unit
and end-to-end tests as guardrails. The story is in [docs/how-it-was-built.md](docs/how-it-was-built.md). Litpage is a
research and demonstration project and is provided as is.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Please run `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` before ope

# TokenBar

**Every AI quota, one glance away.**
An open-source, cross-platform monitor for AI usage limits, balances and reset times.
Runs on **Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS**.

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[CI](https://github.com/lwh0630/TokenBar/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[Release](https://github.com/lwh0630/TokenBar/releases/latest)
[License: MIT](LICENSE)
Platforms
Flutter
Providers

> Inspired by [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) for macOS. TokenBar brings the same idea to Windows, Android, Linux and iOS (and ships a macOS build too), and covers 50 services.

## Why TokenBar

- **See everything in one place.** Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, z.ai and 44 more: remaining quota, balance, reset countdown and whether you are burning through it faster than a linear pace.
- **Nothing sits in the middle.** The app queries each provider's own endpoint from your device. The optional sync server only ever receives usage *snapshots*, never credentials.
- **Reuses what you already have.** On desktop it reads the login your official CLI or app already stored (read-only). Elsewhere you paste an API key or cookie. TokenBar never asks for a password and never logs in on your behalf.
- **Native desktop feel.** A tray icon whose two bars follow your tightest quota, and a compact tray panel that lists every account.

## Screenshots

> **The screenshots use fictional demo data.**

**Desktop**

**Mobile**

> The app interface is available in Simplified Chinese and English. Switch in **Settings → Language**; the default follows your system language (Chinese systems get Chinese, everything else gets English). Text that comes from the provider integrations (setup hints, some field names and error messages) is still Chinese for now, see the [roadmap](#roadmap). Provider names, plan names and numbers are shown as the providers report them.

## Features

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Quota windows** | 5-hour, weekly, monthly and per-model windows, with percent left, reset countdown, local reset time and a pace marker ("ahead of / behind a linear pace", projected usage at reset). |
| **Balances and spend** | Credit balances, spend and caps in the provider's own currency or credit unit. |
| **Tray icon and panel** *(desktop)* | A two-bar tray icon driven by the tightest window, a click-to-open panel for all accounts, right-click menu. The same window doubles as the panel. |
| **Usage history** | Stacked bars per time slot (24 h / 7 d / 30 d), broken down by quota window or by cost item, with each item's share and total. |
| **Notifications** | Low-quota alerts at thresholds you choose and an alert when a low quota resets. |
| **Languages** | Simplified Chinese and English. Choose in **Settings → Language**; defaults to the system language. |
| **Light and dark themes** | Follows the system or set manually. |
| **Phone widgets** | Native Android home-screen widget. iOS WidgetKit sources are included but unverified. |
| **Update check** | Looks for a newer GitHub release at launch (can be turned off) or on demand. See [Updates](#updates). |
| **Optional sync server** | Self-hosted. Push snapshots from your PC, view them on your phone or in the browser. |
| **CLI** | `tokenbar usage` prints the same data in a terminal or as JSON. |

## Supported services

Three ways to read a service:

- **Local login**: reuses the login of the official client already on the machine (read-only). Desktop only.
- **API key / token**: paste it once. Works on desktop, phone and web. On desktop, an empty field falls back to the provider's usual environment variable.
- **Cookie**: copy the `Cookie` request header from your browser's developer tools. These endpoints are not public and may change without notice.

### Subscriptions (local login)

| Service | How it is read | What you see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex (ChatGPT) | `~/.codex/auth.json` (run `codex login` first); falls back to `codex app-server` when the token expired | 5-hour, weekly, credits |
| Claude (Pro / Max) | Claude Code login (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, Keychain on macOS) | 5-hour, weekly, Opus / Sonnet weekly, extra usage |
| Cursor | Cursor desktop login (read-only `state.vscdb`) or a pasted cursor.com cookie | Monthly quota, Auto / API split, on-demand usage |

  Official API keys (23)

| Service | What you see |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI API | Spend over the last 30 days (organization admin key; other keys try the legacy balance endpoint) |
| DeepSeek | Account balance |
| Moonshot / Kimi platform | Account balance |
| xAI | Balance and spend (management key + team ID) |
| Venice | DIEM / USD balance |
| DeepInfra | Balance, month-to-date spend, spend limit |
| Fireworks AI | Spend over the last 30 days |
| Hugging Face | Billing usage (token with billing read access; desktop can read the token saved by `hf auth login`) |
| ElevenLabs | Character quota, voice slots |
| Vercel AI Gateway | Team credits or personal budget |
| Atlas Cloud | Account balance |
| OpenRouter | Credit balance, key limit |
| Tavily | Plan and key credit usage |
| Linkup | Prepaid credit balance |
| Exa | Month-to-date spend of a key (Team Management service key) |
| fal | Credit balance (billing read access) |
| Soniox | Month-to-date usage and budget (organization key) |
| Poe | Remaining points |
| Neuralwatt | Subscription kWh quota, key limit, prepaid balance |
| ZenMux | 5-hour / 7-day quota, pay-as-you-go balance (management key) |
| Warp | AI request quota, bonus credits |
| Synthetic | Rolling, weekly and search quotas |
| Chutes | 4-hour rolling and monthly quotas |

  Coding plans (8)

| Service | What you see |
| --- | --- |
| z.ai / Zhipu GLM | 5-hour and weekly quota, MCP quota (international and China sites) |
| Kimi Code | Weekly / 5-hour / monthly quota (China site by default, region selectable) |
| MiniMax | Interval and weekly quota (China site by default, region selectable) |
| v0 | Billing balance, API rate limits |
| DevPass | Plan credits, weekly premium quota, key spend |
| xKiro | Daily free token quota (resets at 00:00 UTC) |
| ai& | Spend over the last 30 days |
| Groq | Request and token rate over the last 5 minutes (Groq does not publish remaining quota) |

  Self-hosted gateways (6)

| Service | What you see |
| --- | --- |
| LiteLLM | Personal / team budget and spend (virtual key) |
| sub2api | Daily / weekly / monthly quota and rate-limit windows |
| Bifrost | Budget usage |
| LLM Proxy | `quota-stats` (the group with the least remaining) |
| ClawRouter | Monthly budget |
| Aixy | Budget applying to the key |

  Other account APIs (10)

| Service | What you see |
| --- | --- |
| Aerostack | Monthly AI token quota (account JWT) |
| Cosmic AI | Input / output token quota of a project |
| FLORA | Available balance, month-to-date spend |
| Future AGI | AI credits of the billing period, gateway request quota |
| GitKraken AI | Weekly AI credits |
| Sail Research | Organization credit balance, recent spend |
| Munito | Daily / monthly spend limits |
| Sofya | Available / plan / purchased credits |
| Chatbox AI | Plan / bonus / top-up / image quota (license key) |
| IBM Bob | Bobcoin budget per team |

  Not supported, and why

| Service | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| Doubao (Volcano Ark) | The API-key route would have to send a real chat request to probe the quota (it spends tokens); the AK/SK route needs Volcengine request signing |
| AWS Bedrock | Needs AWS SigV4 request signing |
| Vertex AI | Needs a Google Cloud service account / gcloud credentials and signing |
| Azure OpenAI | Needs Azure subscription management credentials |
| Muse (Meta Muse Code) | The only quota endpoint creates an inference key on the account, which is not a read-only operation |
| Antigravity, Grok, Wayfinder, Pi, CodeRabbit | Rely on decrypting browser cookie stores, the macOS keychain or non-public login flows |

Each provider reads documented or reverse-documented endpoints taken from CodexBar's research. Nothing is invented: if an endpoint cannot be traced to its source, it is not shipped.

## Privacy and security

- **Credentials stay on your device**, in the platform secure store (`flutter_secure_storage`). They never go into logs, snapshots or the sync server, and they are not part of any exported JSON.
- **Read-only by default.** TokenBar never refreshes or rewrites another tool's tokens (refreshing rotates the refresh token and can sign the official client out). Refreshing Claude's token is an explicit opt-in setting, off by default.
- **No passwords, no simulated logins.** Only an existing local login, or a key / cookie that you paste yourself.
- **The sync server is optional** and only receives usage snapshots.
- **The update check is one anonymous request** to the GitHub API. See [Updates](#updates).

## Install

Download the latest build from the [**Releases**](https://github.com/lwh0630/TokenBar/releases/latest) page and check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

### Windows 10 / 11 (x64 and ARM64)

1. Download `tokenbar- -windows-x64-setup.exe` (Intel / AMD) or `tokenbar- -windows-arm64-setup.exe` (Windows on ARM) and run it.
2. The installer is per-user by default (no administrator rights, installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\TokenBar`); the privileges dialog lets you install for all users instead. It adds a Start menu entry (and an optional desktop icon), upgrades in place and can be removed from **Settings → Apps**. The Visual C++ runtime is bundled. For silent installs use `/VERYSILENT`.

> The installer and the app are not code-signed. SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC": choose **More info → Run anyway**. Systems that enforce Smart App Control or an application-control policy can block unsigned executables outright. In that case, [build from source](#build-from-source).

### Android 7.0+ (API 24+)

1. Download the APK for your device: `arm64-v8a` for almost every recent phone, `armeabi-v7a` for old 32-bit devices, `x86_64` for emulators.
2. Open it and allow installation from your browser or file manager when Android asks.

APKs are signed with the TokenBar release key. To verify:

```bash
apksigner verify --print-certs tokenbar- -android-arm64-v8a.apk
# certificate SHA-256 digest: c04373ec39a24dd04d6f6797ed984be27d172c01fc30833f957845bb5b622d27
```

### macOS 12+

1. Download `tokenbar- -macos-arm64.dmg` (Apple Silicon: M1 and later) or `tokenbar- -macos-x86_64.dmg` (Intel), open it and drag **TokenBar** to **Applications**.
2. If macOS blocks the first launch, right-click the app and choose **Open**, or run:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/TokenBar.app
```

### Linux x64 / ARM64 — experimental

1. Download `tokenbar- -linux-x64.tar.gz` (Intel / AMD) or `tokenbar- -linux-arm64.tar.gz` (ARM, for example Raspberry Pi 4/5 or Asahi Linux) and extract it.
2. Run `./token_bar` inside the extracted folder.

Runtime libraries: GTK 3, `libsecret` (credential storage, with a running keyring such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet) and `libayatana-appindicator3` (tray icon). On Debian / Ubuntu: `sudo apt install libgtk-3-0 libsecret-1-0 libayatana-appindicator3-1`. On GNOME the tray icon needs the AppIndicator extension. Linux tray icons only offer a menu (no click event), so the compact tray panel is not available there: use the menu's **Open TokenBar**.

### iOS 15+ — experimental, sideload only

`tokenbar- -ios-unsigned.ipa` is **not signed**, and there is no Apple Developer account behind this project, so the file cannot be installed as is. Re-sign and install it with your own Apple ID through a sideloading tool such as [AltStore](https://altstore.io) or [Sideloadly](https://sideloadly.io) (free Apple IDs have to renew the install every 7 days). The Home Screen widget is not part of the IPA.

### Platform status

| Platform | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Windows x64 | Supported. Built and tested on Windows 11; CI builds a release on every push. |
| Windows ARM64 | Experimental. Built natively on a Windo

#  Omnigent

### The open-source meta-harness for all your AI agents.

Omnigent is an open-source **meta-harness** that gives you a common orchestration layer over Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Hermes, Pi, and the agents you write yourself: swap or combine harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in real time from any device — terminal, browser, phone, or the native desktop app.

[PyPI version](https://pypi.org/project/omnigent/)
[License: Apache 2.0](https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent/blob/main/LICENSE)
[Discord](https://discord.gg/omnigent)
Status: alpha

[omnigent.ai](https://omnigent.ai) · **[⬇️ Download the macOS desktop app](https://omnigent.ai/quickstart/install#install-the-desktop-app)**

---

## Why Omnigent?

Omnigent lets you:

- **📱 Work with agents from any device, including your phone.** Sessions
  follow you: start in your terminal, continue in the browser, pick it up on
  your phone. Messages, sub-agents, terminals, and files stay in sync.

- **🤖 Supervise multiple agents.** Mix Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode,
  Hermes, Pi, and custom agents (defined in YAML) together in the same
  session. Ask one agent to review another's work, or split a task across
  agents that are each good at different things.

- **🔌 Use any model.** A first-party API key, a Claude/ChatGPT subscription,
  or any compatible gateway. All first-class.

- **🤝 Collaborate.** Share a session so teammates can chat with your agent
  and watch it work live, co-drive it on your machine, or fork the
  conversation to continue on their own.

- **☁️ Run agents in cloud sandboxes.** No laptop required: run sessions in
  disposable [Modal](https://modal.com), [Daytona](https://www.daytona.io),
  [Blaxel](https://blaxel.ai),
  [Islo](https://islo.dev), [E2B](https://e2b.dev),
  [Gensee](https://gensee.ai),
  [CoreWeave](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/sandboxes),
  [Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io), [OpenShell](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell),
  [Boxlite](https://github.com/boxlite-ai/boxlite),
  [microsandbox](https://github.com/superradcompany/microsandbox), or
  [Databricks](https://www.databricks.com) sandboxes, launched from the
  CLI or provisioned by the server per session (*managed hosts*).

- **🛡️ Govern your agents.** Create
  [policies](#6-govern-your-agents-with-policies) to pause for your approval
  before risky actions, cap spend, or limit which tools an agent reaches.
  They apply to the whole server, one agent, or a single chat.

---

## Quick start

### 1. Install

One command installs Omnigent and everything it needs:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent/main/scripts/install_oss.sh | sh
```

The installer includes Databricks support and installs the Databricks CLI
alongside Omnigent, or reuses an existing CLI that supports workspace login.
Pass `--no-databricks` to omit them.

 Optional integrations and extras

Need an optional integration? Pass one or more extras to the installer:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent/main/scripts/install_oss.sh | sh -s -- --extra modal,e2b
```

The Antigravity SDK extra conflicts with Databricks dependencies. Install it
with `--no-databricks --extra antigravity`.

Available user-facing extras include:

- **Model providers:** `databricks` (included by default), `bedrock`, `vertex`
- **Sandbox providers:** `modal`, `daytona`, `blaxel`, `boxlite`, `microsandbox`,
  `cwsandbox`, `e2b`, `openshell`, `kubernetes`
- **SDK harnesses:** `antigravity`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `agents-sdk`
- **Storage and memory:** `s3`, `hindsight`

 Prefer to install manually?

Omnigent needs **Python 3.12+**. Install the `omnigent` package:

```bash
uv tool install omnigent        # or: pip install "omnigent"
```

Manual installs use the same extras syntax, for example:

```bash
uv tool install "omnigent[databricks,modal]"
```

Or with [Homebrew](https://github.com/omnigent-ai/homebrew-tap):

```bash
brew install omnigent-ai/tap/omnigent
```

For source builds on networks that require package mirrors, replace these example
URLs with your mirrors:

```bash
HOMEBREW_PIP_INDEX_URL='https://pypi.example.com/simple' \
HOMEBREW_CARGO_INDEX_URL='https://cargo.example.com/index/' \
  brew install --build-from-source omnigent-ai/tap/omnigent
```

The PyPI setting also routes pip's isolated build dependencies through the mirror.
The Cargo setting takes a sparse registry index URL ending in `/`, without the
`sparse+` prefix. Both overrides are optional and do not affect prebuilt-bottle
installs.

Or install straight from the repo:

```bash
uv tool install -q --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent.git
```

 Toolchain and prerequisites (if the installer reports a missing tool)

- **`uv`** (required). https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/
  The installer offers to set this up for you.
- **`git`** (required).
- **Node.js 22 LTS or newer** with **`npm`** (for the coding-harness CLIs
  installed by `omnigent run`) and **`pnpm`** (for the web UI). You can get
  both from a single Node install; pnpm is available via
  `corepack enable` or `npm install -g pnpm`.
- **Devin CLI** (optional), for `omnigent devin`: install with
  `curl -fsSL https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash`, then sign in with
  `devin auth login`. Devin tool approvals appear as Chat approval cards
  (its `PermissionRequest` hook is mirrored to the web UI) and stay
  answerable in the embedded Terminal. See `docs/devin-native.md`.
- **Kiro CLI** (optional), for `omnigent kiro`: install with
  `curl -fsSL https://cli.kiro.dev/install | bash`, then sign in with Kiro.
  Kiro tool approvals stay answerable in the embedded Terminal; supported
  one-time approvals also appear as Chat cards. See
  `docs/kiro-native-elicitation.md`.
- **`tmux`**, required by the native `omnigent  ` terminal wrappers
  (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `devin`, `hermes`, `kiro`, `pi`)
  (`brew install tmux` / `apt install tmux`; the installer offers
  to install it for you).
- **`bubblewrap`** (`bwrap`), **Linux only**. The native `omnigent  `
  terminal wrappers and the `pi` harness wrap each agent
  terminal in a `bwrap` OS-sandbox; on Linux that isolation is mandatory, so a
  missing `bwrap` binary makes those terminals fail to start
  (`apt install bubblewrap`; the installer offers to install it for you). macOS
  uses the built-in `seatbelt` sandbox and needs nothing extra.
- **Databricks.** The bootstrap installer includes the `databricks` extra
  and the Databricks CLI. If installing with uv directly, use
  `uv tool install "omnigent[databricks]"` and install the
  [Databricks CLI](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/cli/install)
  separately. Sign in to a workspace-hosted server with
  `omnigent login  /omnigent`.

 Windows (native)

Omnigent runs natively on Windows in a degraded mode. The `install_oss.sh`
bootstrap is POSIX-only, so install with `uv` directly:

```powershell
uv tool install --python 3.12 omnigent
# or from the repo:
uv tool install --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent.git
```

What works on Windows: `omnigent server`, the web UI, and the SDK-based
harnesses (`omnigent run  ` with the claude-sdk / cursor / codex
harnesses). Agents run under a Windows **Job Object** for process-tree
containment.

What is **not** available on Windows (use Linux/macOS, or WSL, for these):

- the native `omnigent claude` / `omnigent codex` / `omnigent cursor`
  tmux/PTY terminal wrappers (run an SDK harness or the web UI instead);
- `bwrap`/`seatbelt` filesystem & network sandboxing and the L7 egress proxy
  — the Job Object backend contains the process tree and enforces resource
  limits but does **not** isolate the filesystem or network.

 Updating to a new release

When a newer release is on PyPI, Omnigent shows a one-line notice (once per
release) pointing here. To update:

```bash
omni upgrade            # detects how you installed, drains & stops the local
                        # server, then runs the matching upgrade command
omni upgrade --check    # just report whether a newer release is available
```

`omni upgrade` waits for in-flight agent sessions to finish before stopping the
local server (pass `--force` to stop them immediately); the next `omni` command
brings the server back up on the new version. Source checkouts update with
`git pull` instead. Silence the notice with `OMNIGENT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`.

The check queries your configured package index — honoring `UV_INDEX_URL` /
`PIP_INDEX_URL` and your `uv.toml` / `pip.conf` (default PyPI), so private
mirrors work out of the box; override with `OMNIGENT_INDEX_URL` if needed.

 Uninstalling Omnigent

Preview the CLI/profile cleanup that would run by default:

```bash
omnigent uninstall
```

Remove the CLI and installer-managed PATH entries while keeping your local
history, credentials, and projects:

```bash
omnigent uninstall --yes
```

To also remove Omnigent state under `~/.omnigent`, pass `--purge`; Omnigent
backs it up outside the target before deletion. Your `~/omnigent` workspace is
kept unless you explicitly add `--purge-workspace`.

```bash
omnigent uninstall --purge --yes
```

If the installed wheel is broken or `omnigent` is not on `PATH`, run the
standalone script instead:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent/main/scripts/uninstall_oss.sh | sh
```

Add `--yes` to the standalone script to perform the previewed CLI cleanup.

### 2. Start your first agent

`omnigent` picks a model with you and starts a session in your terminal. It
also launches a local web UI at `http://localhost:6767` that shows the same
session in the browser, or on a phone on your network (step 4). The
[desktop app](https://omnigent.ai/docs/interact/desktop) wraps that same UI
in a native window and adds OS notifications (with a configurable sound) and a dock badge —
[download it for macOS](https://omnigent.ai/quickstart/install#install-the-desktop-app).

> [!NOTE]
> The install puts two names for the same CLI on your PATH: `omnigent` and
> the shorter `omni`. They're interchangeable.

> [!TIP]
> On first run, Omnigent picks up model credentials already in your
> environment (an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or a `claude` /
> `codex` CLI you're logged into) and offers one as the default.

```bash
omnigent
```

Or launch a specific agent runtime:

```bash
omnigent claude                      # Claude Code, in a session your team can join
omnigent codex                       # Codex
omnigent cursor                      # Cursor
omnigent agy                         # Antigravity
omnigent opencode                    # OpenCode
omnigent hermes                      # Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
omnigent pi                          # Pi
omnigent copilot                     # GitHub Copilot (SDK harness, via `omnigent run`)
```

`omnigent agy` requires agy 1.1.13 or newer. When `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set,
direct Gemini API authentication takes precedence over agy's saved OAuth login.

To configure native agy credentials, run `omni setup` →
**Antigravity** → **Configure native agy API key / gateway** → **Add a credential**
and choose the option matching your connection:

- **Gemini — API key** for a Google AI Studio key.
- **Gemini API gateway — URL + key** for an external gateway implementing native
  Gemini requests and `x-goog-api-key` authentication. Supply its API root, such
  as `https://gateway.example/gemini`, without `/v1beta` or a model operation.
- **Databricks — profile** for a Databricks workspace with native Gemini API
  access. Omnigent manages profile authentication and model-name mapping; no
  workspace URL or token needs to be pasted into the gateway form.

repositories.description: Build AI phone agents on your own computer and test every change with an AI caller. Open source, runs free with no API keys, cents per call with your own keys. Imports Dialogflow CX.
repositories.readmeExcerpt:
Open-source, self-hosted voice agents.

  Bring your agents over from  Dialogflow CX  and  CX Agent Studio , or start fresh.
  Build, test and run them on your own machine or servers, in one command,
  for about $0.02–0.17 a call instead of $0.50.

    🚀 Quick start    · 
   📋 Free phone evals   · 
   🔁 Import from Google   · 
   👀 Tour   · 
   🧠 Models   · 
   📞 Phone and SIP   · 
   🗺️ Roadmap   · 
   📘 Engine docs   · 
   🧩  vk  CLI

    Import a Dialogflow CX agent, test it, and grade a real phone call to it. Sample agent and made-up data; replies from Lampline's test model.

Lampline imports your Dialogflow CX and CX Agent Studio agents, flows, pages,
playbooks, forms and tools included, and runs them on hardware you control. It gives
you a drag-and-drop builder where LLM steps and scripted pages mix in one agent, a test console that lights up each step as the call moves, HTTP and
MCP tools, records and document search of its own, and phone calls over Twilio,
Telnyx or any SIP trunk through jambonz. Built on
[Pipecat](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat).

      🏠 Local first  One command on a laptop, a GPU box or an on-prem server. No cloud account needed.
      🔒 Private by default  No telemetry, bound to localhost, a key on every request, and keys never in your agents or the repo.

      🧠 Any model  Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, Grok and more, or Ollama on your own hardware.
      🧩 Agents as code  Every agent is a folder of YAML and Markdown: reviewed in git, tested with  vk , exported back to Google's tools whenever you like.

## 📋 Test any phone agent for free

Lampline's **Evals** tab phones a voice agent over a real phone line, plays the
caller with an AI **Test Caller**, and grades the call against what should
happen. It works on any agent with a phone number: one built in Lampline,
Dialogflow CX, CX Agent Studio, Vapi, Retell, or your IVR.

- **Free calls through Google Voice.** The Lampline Phone Bridge extension (Chrome or Edge) connects the call's audio to the Test Caller inside the browser: no cables, Windows or Mac. Or use any phone on speaker.
- **Graded, with reasons.** You write who is calling, what they want and what must happen; your model grades the transcript, check by check. A call that heard nothing shows *Didn't run*, never *Failed*.
- **Tough callers.** Background noise, accents, interruptions, long pauses, hesitant or rambling speech.
- **The agent's speed, as callers hear it.** Typical and p95 response time, phone line included.
- **Bring your test scripts.** Paste Hammer, Cyara or spreadsheet tests and they become runnable cases. Replay any failed call.

[How to run evals →](docs/EVALS.md)

Only call agents you own or are allowed to test. You press Call yourself:
Google Voice doesn't allow automated dialing.

## 🔁 Bring your Dialogflow CX and CX Agent Studio agents

Export an agent from Google's console, drop the .zip on **New agent → Import**, and
it opens in the builder: flows, pages, forms, routes, playbooks and tools carried
over, with a report of anything to check before it takes calls. It works the
other way too: **Export** writes any agent back as a Dialogflow CX package or a
CX Agent Studio app.

        📥 Import.  A Dialogflow CX package or a CX Agent Studio app (JSON or YAML). The conversion runs on your computer and never runs code from the export.

        ✏️ Ready to edit.  Pages become scripted pages, playbooks become LLM steps, flows group them, and webhooks and OpenAPI tools become tools.

| From Dialogflow CX | Becomes |
|---|---|
| Flows and pages | Flows of [scripted pages](engine/README.md#scripted-pages-and-flows): entry messages said word for word |
| Form parameters, entity types | Form fields with their types, choices and synonyms, patterns and keypad input |
| Intent and condition routes, no-match handlers | Transfers the model decides, rules, and "no match" transfers |
| Playbooks | LLM steps with their goal, guidelines and steps |
| Webhooks, OpenAPI tools, data store tools | Tools (webhooks answer with a mock until connected) and local knowledge search |

| From CX Agent Studio | Becomes |
|---|---|
| Root agent and child agents | A root agent with sub-agents and transfers both ways |
| Global instruction, variables | Global instructions and context variables |
| OpenAPI toolsets, Python tools, data stores | HTTP tools, tools with example answers, and local knowledge search |

From the terminal: `vk import auto export.zip` and `vk export dfcx|ces agents/ `.
The full mapping, both ways, and what doesn't carry over yet:
[cli/README.md](cli/README.md#import).

## 👀 A quick tour

    Sample data only.

        🧪 Test calls.  Chat or talk through your microphone. The steps light up as the call moves, and every collected detail shows on the right.

        🧠 20 model providers.  Pick one, paste a key, press Test connection. Speech runs in the cloud or free on your own computer.

        📞 Phone calls and SIP.  Twilio, Telnyx, or your own SIP trunk, PBX or SBC through jambonz. Genesys, Avaya, Cisco and more are coming.

        🗄️ Data of its own.  Collections agents look up and save during calls, and document search over your FAQs, all on your machine.

 Screenshots use the bundled sample agents and made-up data.

## 🏠 Where it runs

| | Status | |
|---|---|---|
| **Local and on-prem** | ✅ Available | One Docker container, or the engine natively, on any machine you control |
| **Google Cloud** | 🔜 Coming soon | A one-command deployment to your own Google Cloud project |

## 🚀 Quick start

Needs Docker with Compose v2 (Docker Desktop is fine). **No API keys or accounts:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/C4rohan/lampline && cd lampline
scripts/docker-up.sh --free          # everything on this computer: Ollama, Moonshine and Kokoro
```

`--free` runs the model (Qwen3 4B in Ollama) and speech (Moonshine listening,
Kokoro speaking) on your own computer. The first start downloads about 3 GB and
shows progress; after that it starts in seconds. Replies are slower and simpler
than a cloud model's, and you can switch to any provider on the Integrations
page whenever you like. On a Mac, the native route is faster, because Ollama
uses the GPU outside Docker: install [Ollama](https://ollama.com), then
`scripts/engine-up.sh --free`.

Have API keys? Run `scripts/docker-up.sh` without `--free`. Either way it prints
a link like `http://localhost:7860/#/?key=…`: open it once and the page
remembers the key. Pick your model and voice on the Integrations page (or put keys like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` in
`.env`; see `.env.example`). Your agents are in `./agents` (edit them, keep them
in git) and everything else the engine keeps, settings with your keys, records,
knowledge and downloaded models, is in `./.vpe-data`.
`scripts/docker-up.sh --down` stops it; `--logs` follows its log. Plain
`docker compose up -d --build` works too once `.env` has `VPE_DOCKER_API_KEY`.
Details: [engine/README.md](engine/README.md#docker).

Prefer no Docker? `scripts/engine-up.sh` runs the engine natively (Python 3.11+)
at http://localhost:7860, which also lets browser calls reach it directly.
Free, private speech: Integrations → Whisper and Kokoro → **Download models**,
or Moonshine for listening, which transcribes while the caller talks.

## 🧠 Models

Pick one on the Integrations page; each starts on a sensible default model you
can change, and **Test connection** checks the key.

| Provider | Key |
|---|---|
| Claude (Anthropic) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint | `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `VPE_LLM_BASE_URL` |
| Gemini | `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| Gemini on Vertex AI | `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` plus a service account key or this computer's Google credentials |
| Azure OpenAI | `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` |
| Amazon Bedrock | AWS keys, or this computer's AWS credentials |
| Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, Grok (xAI), Together AI, Fireworks AI, OpenRouter, Cerebras, NVIDIA NIM, Qwen, SambaNova, Nebius, Novita AI | each provider's API key |
| Ollama | none: open models on this computer or your own server |

## 📞 Phone calls and SIP

| | |
|---|---|
| Twilio | a Twilio number rings your agent; outbound calls from triggers |
| Telnyx | the same, through a TeXML application |
| SIP through [jambonz](https://jambonz.org) | any SIP trunk, PBX or session border controller: point a jambonz application at the engine |

The Phone numbers page has the webhook to copy and the steps for each.
Details: [engine/README.md](engine/README.md#phone-calls-twilio-telnyx-or-sip).

### 🏢 Contact centers (coming soon)

Genesys Cloud, Avaya, Cisco Webex Contact Center, Cisco UCCE and PCCE, Amazon
Connect, NICE CXone, Five9 and Twilio Flex show on the Integrations page as
coming soon. Until each lands, most of them can already send calls to your
agents over a SIP trunk through jambonz. The plan for each:
[docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md#contact-centers-coming-soon).

## ⚙️ How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  you((You)) --> app[Lampline app builder, tests, integrations :7860]
  app --> engine[Engine Pipecat pipelines]
  phone((Callers)) --> carriers[Twilio · Telnyx · SIP via jambonz]
  carriers --> engine
  engine --> agents[(agents/ YAML + Markdown)]
  engine --> data[(Records and knowledge, SQLite)]
  engine --> models{{Model and speech cloud APIs or local Whisper · Moonshine · Parakeet · Kokoro · Qwen3-TTS · Ollama}}
  engine -- tools --> hooks[Your APIs and MCP servers]
```

The engine reads the agent folders on every call, so a change is live on the
next call. Settings and keys live in a `chmod 600` file outside the repo.

## 💰 What a voice-agent call actually costs

Monthly totals for 4-minute calls at list prices (October 2026). Staff time is
not included. Reproduce or change any assumption with `python3 costs/cost_model.py`.

| Deployment | 10k calls/mo | 50k calls/mo | 200k calls/mo |
|---|---|---|---|
| CX Agent Studio (list price, baseline) | $5,000 | $25,000 | $100,000 |
| On-prem server (no GPU) + Google model APIs | $1,384 | $6,235 | $24,426 |
| On-prem GPU servers + self-hosted models | $681 | $1,363 | $3,748 |
| Cloud Run + Google model APIs (coming soon) | $1,423 | $6,356 | $24,908 |
| GKE production + mixed vendors: Deepgram, Claude Haiku, Fish Audio (coming soon) | $1,105 | $3,612 | $13,037 |
| GKE production + self-hosted models on L4 GPUs, 3-yr CUD (coming soon) | $1,054 | $1,675 | $3,888 |

What the numbers say:
- 📉 **Hosting is the small part.** Model APIs are almost the whole bill, so the model choice matters far more than local vs. cloud.
- 🖥️ **Self-hosted models are where the big savings are,** but they rest on two assumptions nobody has published good data for: concurrent calls per GPU, and whether an 8B open model is good enough for your flows. [Help measure them](CONTRIBUTING.md).

Every row, per-call figures and assumptions: [costs/COSTS.md](costs/COSTS.md).

## 🧩 Agents as code (`vk`)

Build and change agents from a terminal or an AI coding agent as well as the
builder. Each agent is a folder: `agent.yaml` for the graph and one Markdown
file per prompt, so changes are reviewable in git.

```bash
pip install -e cli                  # installs the `vk` command
vk templates install front-desk     # start from a ready-made agent
vk lint agents/front-desk           # graph checks + a scan for real-looking patient data
vk test agents/front-desk           # runs tests/*.yaml conversations on the engine
vk import dfcx export.zip           # bring an agent over from Dialogflow CX or CX Agent Studio
vk skills install --target claude   # builder + reviewer skills for Claude Code
```

Details in [cli/README.md](cli/README.md). The engine itself, its builder,
tools, data and knowledge: [engine/README.md](engine/README.md).

## 🗺

English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) | [日本語](README_ja.md)

[VectorVein](https://vectorvein.ai)

# 🔀 VectorVein

Build your automation workflow with the power of AI and your personal knowledge base.

Create powerful workflows with just drag and drop, without any programming.

[Online Version of VectorVein](https://github.com/AndersonBY/vector-vein)

VectorVein is a no-code AI workflow software inspired by [LangChain](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain) and [langflow](https://github.com/logspace-ai/langflow), designed to combine the powerful capabilities of large language models and enable users to easily achieve intelligent and automated workflows for various daily tasks.

## 🌐 Online Experience

You can experience VectorVein's online version [here](https://vectorvein.ai/en), with no need to download or install.

Official website [Online Documentation](https://vectorvein.ai/help/docs/introduction)

## 📦 Installation and Configuration

### Installation

After downloading VectorVein from [Release](https://github.com/AndersonBY/vector-vein/releases/), the program will create a "data" folder in the installation directory to store the database and static file resources.

VectorVein is built using pywebview, based on the webview2 kernel, so you need to install the webview2 runtime. If the software cannot be opened, you may need to download the webview2 runtime manually from [https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If the software cannot be opened after decompression, please check if the downloaded compressed package .zip file is locked. You can solve this problem by right-clicking the compressed package and selecting "Unblock".

### Configuration

Most workflows and agents in the software involve the use of AI large language models, so you should at least provide a usable configuration for a large language model. For workflows, you can see which large language models are being used in the interface, as shown in the image below.

LLM used in workflow

#### API Endpoint Configuration

Starting from v0.2.10, VectorVein separates API endpoints and large language model configurations, allowing multiple API endpoints for the same large language model.

API Endpoint Configuration

After the software opens normally, click the open settings button, and you can configure the information for each API endpoint as needed, or add custom API endpoints. Currently, the API endpoints support OpenAI-compatible interfaces, which can be connected to locally running services such as LM-Studio, Ollama, vLLM, etc.

> The API Base for LM-Studio is typically http://localhost:1234/v1/
>
> The API Base for Ollama is typically http://localhost:11434/v1/

#### Remote Large Language Model Interface Configuration

Please configure the specific information for each model in the `Remote LLMs` tab.

LLM Settings

Click on any model to set its specific configuration, as shown below.

LLM Settings

> The `Model Key` is the standard name of the large model and generally does not need to be adjusted. The `Model ID` is the name used during actual deployment, which usually matches the `Model Key`. However, in deployments like Azure OpenAI, the `Model ID` is user-defined and therefore needs to be adjusted according to the actual situation.
>
> Since the model IDs from different providers for the same model may vary, you can click the `Edit` button to configure the specific model ID under this endpoint, as shown in the figure below.
>
> Endpoint Model ID Configuration

#### Custom Large Language Model Interface Configuration

If using a custom large language model, fill in the custom model configuration information on the `Custom LLMs` tab. Currently, interfaces compatible with OpenAI are supported, such as LM-Studio, Ollama, vLLM, etc.

Custom LLM Settings

First, add a custom model family, then add a custom model. Don't forget to click the `Save Settings` button.

#### Speech Recognition Configuration

Currently, speech recognition uses the OpenAI-compatible path. You can use the same configuration as the large language model or set up a speech recognition service compatible with the OpenAI API (such as Groq).

Speech Recognition Configuration

### Embedding Configuration

When you need to perform vector searches using vector data, configure embedding backends in the `Embedding models` settings through the `vv-llm` `embedding_backends` scheme. Built-in OpenAI embeddings and custom request/response mappings are supported, so local services such as [text-embeddings-inference](https://github.com/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference) can be connected by configuring endpoints plus request/response mappings.

Local Embedding Settings

### Shortcut Settings

For ease of daily use, you can configure shortcuts to quickly initiate voice conversations with the Agent. By launching through the shortcut, you can directly interact with the Agent via speech recognition. It is important to ensure that the speech recognition service is correctly configured beforehand.

**Include Screenshot** means that while starting the conversation, a screenshot of the screen will be taken and uploaded as an attachment to the conversation.

Shortcut Settings

### Notes

#### About the local Stable Diffusion API

To use your own local Stable Diffusion API, you need to add the parameter --api to the startup item of webui-user.bat, that is

```
set COMMANDLINE_ARGS=--api
```

## 💻 Usage

### 🔌 API Access (New in v0.4.0)

VectorVein now provides a local API service that allows you to call workflows programmatically. This enables integration with other applications and automation tools.

#### API Features

- **Local FastAPI Server**: Runs automatically when VectorVein starts
- **RESTful Interface**: Standard HTTP endpoints for workflow operations
- **Workflow Execution**: Run workflows with custom input parameters
- **Status Monitoring**: Check workflow execution status and results
- **OpenAPI Documentation**: Interactive API documentation at `/docs`

#### API Endpoints

The API service runs on `http://localhost:8787` (default port) and provides the following endpoints:

- `GET /api/info` - Get API server information
- `GET /api/workflow/list` - List all workflows
- `GET /api/workflow/{workflow_id}` - Get workflow details
- `POST /api/workflow/run` - Execute a workflow
- `POST /api/workflow/check-status` - Check workflow execution status
- `GET /health` - Health check endpoint

#### Example Usage

```python
import requests

# Run a workflow
response = requests.post('http://localhost:8787/api/workflow/run', json={
```

A workflow represents a work task process, including input, output, and how input is processed to reach the output result.

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
# kwant

**Your own team of AI bots, in one self-hosted binary.**

[CI](https://github.com/alexsergivan/kwant/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[License: AGPL-3.0](#license)
[Docs](https://kwant.si/docs/quickstart)

kwant gives you a team of bots that share chats, hand work to each other with an @mention and get it done on their own, on a schedule or while you're away. Keep separate spaces for work and home, each with its own bots and accounts. Run it on your laptop or a server, with the Claude, Codex or Grok CLI you already use, or your own API keys.

It's written in Rust (Tokio, Axum, SQLite) with a React web app embedded in the binary.

A kwant channel: Designer answers a question about empty states, then @mentions QA, and QA checks it on a 360 pixel screen.

**Website and docs: [kwant.si](https://kwant.si)** · **[Download for Mac](https://github.com/alexsergivan/kwant/releases/latest/download/kwant_universal.dmg)**

---

## Why kwant

- **A team, not a chat tab.** Each bot has its own role, voice ("soul") and model. Bots @mention each other to hand work on, a team lead runs short discussions and posts one summary, and the [Laya](#laya-model-router) router picks who answers and with which model and effort.
- **Spaces.** Separate spaces for work, a side project and home. Each has its own bots, teams, channels, routines, accounts, approval rule and hiring rule.
- **Every account you have.** Several accounts per engine: Claude, Codex or Grok CLI logins, Anthropic, OpenAI or xAI keys, and your own OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible server. Set a default and a priority order. When an account runs out of usage, the turn moves to the next one and the chat says so. You can pin a bot to one account.
- **Works while you're away.** Routines on a schedule (bots can set them up when you ask, with an Undo button), follow-ups bots schedule for themselves, and a *While you were away* page with what's waiting on you, what finished and what failed.
- **Autonomous, with a safety net you control.** Ordinary work runs without stopping. On *Ask only when risky*, the default for new spaces, only risky steps such as `git push`, network calls, unknown commands or changes outside the bot's folder show an approval card with the exact command: *Allow once*, *Always allow* or *Deny*. Per space or per bot, switch to ask every time or don't ask.
- **Loose ends and letters.** kwant reads your chats and, if you add them, an IMAP inbox and your GitHub issues and pull requests, read-only, and finds what you started and never finished. Photograph a bill or a form and it pulls out the sender, the ask and the deadline and drafts a reply. It never sends anything.
- **Parallel Universe.** Compare up to three ways to deploy an app with local container tests and dated price estimates. Every number is tagged as verified, an estimate or speculation. No cloud account and no spending.
- **No telemetry.** kwant sends nothing to us, and its interface loads nothing from other servers. The one download you don't set up yourself is the [Laya](#laya-model-router) router on first start: its Python packages and its model from PyPI and Hugging Face (`--no-laya` turns it off). Everything else goes only to the AI providers and services you add.
- **And more:** memory and skills per bot (you approve new skills), bots that propose hiring a teammate, import a bot from a Claude Code subagent, a SKILL.md, a character card or a JSON export, search across a space's chats, MCP tool servers, a shared browser for bots, saved passwords with an optional Bitwarden store, and Local or VM computer mode.

See every feature, with screenshots, on [kwant.si/features](https://kwant.si/features).

        Spaces : each with its own bots, channels and routines.
        Accounts : several per engine, with a default and fallbacks.

        Approvals : see exactly what a bot wants to run.
        Routines : ask for "every morning" and get one, with Undo.

        While you were away : what's waiting, finished or failed.
        Loose ends : evidence and a draft. It never sends.

Screenshots come from a demo space with sample data.

---

## Quickstart

### What you need

- **Rust** (stable), installed with [rustup](https://rustup.rs).
- **Node.js 20 or newer** with npm, to build the web app. The finished binary doesn't need it.
- **At least one AI account.** Any one of these is enough:
  - the [`claude`](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) CLI, installed. You don't need to sign it in first: kwant has a **Sign in with Claude** button;
  - the `codex` or `grok` CLI, signed in on the same machine (`codex login`, `grok login`);
  - an Anthropic, OpenAI or xAI API key, which you add in the app under **Space settings → Accounts**.
- Optional: **Docker** for VM mode and the bots' shared browser, and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) or `python3` for the Laya router.

`kwnt doctor` (`cargo run -- doctor` from a clone) checks all of these and prints the install command for whatever is missing on your machine; `kwnt setup` installs it (see [Without Docker](#without-docker-kwnt-setup)).

### Run from a fresh clone

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alexsergivan/kwant.git
cd kwant
make run          # builds the web app (frontend/dist), then runs `cargo run -- serve`
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8799**. If no account works yet, kwant shows a **Get ready** banner with an **Add an account** button. A fresh install starts with three bots in `#general`: Architect, TechLead and DevOps. Make more with **New bot**, from a ready-made persona or blank.

The binary embeds `frontend/dist`, so on a fresh clone `cargo build`, `cargo test` and `cargo run -- serve` fail to compile until you've run `make run` or `make frontend` once.

**The first start takes a few minutes:** kwant installs its Laya router and downloads its model (about 420 MB) in the background. Bots answer meanwhile, picked by keyword. To skip Laya, run `cargo run -- serve --no-laya`.

### Build a release binary

```bash
make build                 # web app + cargo build --release
./target/release/kwnt serve
```

### On a Mac: the app

[Download the Mac app](https://github.com/alexsergivan/kwant/releases/latest/download/kwant_universal.dmg) (a universal `.dmg` for Apple silicon and Intel) and drag kwant to Applications. It runs its own kwant on your Mac, with the same `~/.kwnt` data folder as `kwnt serve`, and stays in the menu bar when you close the window. Build it yourself from [`apps/mac`](apps/mac/README.md).

The app is signed ad hoc, not notarized by Apple, so macOS stops it the first time. Click **Done**, open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down and click **Open Anyway**. On macOS 14 or earlier, right-click the app and choose **Open** instead.

### Install the web app

In Chrome or Edge, click **Install app** in the sidebar; in Safari on a Mac, **File → Add to Dock**; on a phone, kwant shows how. Browsers only install pages served over https or from `127.0.0.1`.

To get notifications on your phone with kwant closed, install it (on an iPhone, add it to the Home Screen first) and turn on **Settings → Notifications → Notify me on this device**. kwant then sends a Web Push notification for each kind you've ticked there, such as an approval or a question. It goes through your browser's push service (Google's for Chrome on Android, Apple's on an iPhone), encrypted so that service can't read it. Signing a browser out under **Signed-in devices** stops its notifications.

More in the [quickstart](https://kwant.si/docs/quickstart) and [install](https://kwant.si/docs/install) docs.

---

## Self-hosting on a VPS

### The binary

`kwnt` is self-contained: SQLite and the web app are inside it.

```bash
scp target/release/kwnt user@your-vps:/usr/local/bin/kwnt
ssh user@your-vps "kwnt serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8799"
```

On your own computer there is nothing to sign in to. From another machine, open the one-time link `kwnt serve` prints at startup (it works once, for 15 minutes; with `KWNT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` set it is ready to open and comes with a QR code), or make a new one with `kwnt signin-link`. The browser stays signed in for a year. To add your phone or another browser later, open **Settings → Signed-in devices → Add a phone or browser** in a signed-in browser and scan the one-time QR code (it also works once, for 15 minutes); the same list lets you sign those browsers out. A new browser can also choose **Sign in from another device** on the sign-in screen: it shows a code for 10 minutes, and a signed-in browser shows **New device wants access** with Approve or Deny. Approve only a code that is on a screen you are holding. Prefer the token? On the server, as the user that runs kwnt, `cat ~/.kwnt/api-token` (or `$KWNT_DATA_DIR/api-token`, e.g. `sudo cat /var/lib/kwnt/api-token` with the systemd unit below) prints the token to paste (`kwnt token --raw` does the same; `./target/release/kwnt` if kwnt isn't on your PATH), and `kwnt token` prints a new one-time link like `kwnt signin-link`. Run them as the same user: as another user they fail, because that user can't read the token file (for the systemd unit use `sudo cat` as above). Each install has its own token, so one copied from your laptop won't open kwnt on the server. Or skip sign-in: `ssh -N -L 8799:127.0.0.1:8799 user@your-vps`, then open http://127.0.0.1:8799 on your computer (not with Docker, where requests always count as remote). A one-time link signs in as you, so keep it private until you've used it; the token never appears in the server's output. Put a TLS reverse proxy in front: see [browser service and VPS hosting](docs/browser-service.md).

 A systemd unit

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/kwnt.service
[Unit]
Description=kwant AI bot platform
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
# A dedicated user (useradd --system --create-home --home-dir /var/lib/kwnt kwnt); sign the
# claude/codex/grok CLIs in as this user, or add API keys in the app
User=kwnt
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/kwnt serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8799
Restart=always
Environment=KWNT_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/kwnt

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```bash
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now kwnt
```

### VPS in 5 minutes (Docker Compose)

One command starts everything kwant needs: kwnt, **Laya** (picks which bot answers, model baked in) and a private **Chromium** for the bots (VM mode), with no Docker socket mounted. You need Docker with Compose and about 4 GB of free RAM (Chromium is capped at 1.5 GB).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alexsergivan/kwant.git && cd kwant
KWNT_CLIS=claude,codex docker compose up -d --build   # any of claude,codex,grok; leave out for none
docker compose exec kwnt kwnt doctor                  # what works, and the fix for what doesn't
docker compose exec kwnt claude auth login            # sign a CLI in (codex login --device-auth, grok login --device-auth)
docker compose exec kwnt kwnt signin-link            # a one-time sign-in link and QR code (15 minutes)
```

Or skip the CLIs and add an Anthropic, OpenAI or xAI API key in the app under **Space settings → Accounts**. CLI sign-ins live in the `kwnt-home` volume and data in `kwnt-data`, so both survive rebuilds.

**HTTPS:** the UI is published on `127.0.0.1:8799` only. Put a TLS proxy in front, e.g. [Caddy](https://caddyserver.com) with this `Caddyfile`, and tell kwnt its address:

```
kwant.example.com {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8799
}
```

```bash
echo KWNT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://kwant.example.com >> .env && docker compose up -d
```

`docker compose exec kwnt kwnt signin-link` prints a one-time sign-in link for your domain and a QR code to scan with your phone. It works once, for 15 minutes; run it again for the next device. `docker compose exec kwnt kwnt token --raw` still prints the API token, as a fallback.

- **Image sizes** (measured): kwnt alone 0.2 GB; with `KWNT_CLIS=claude,codex,grok` 1.7 GB (the CLIs add about 0.9 GB, so they are off by default). Laya 3.

repositories.description: Anything to API (万物皆可2API): put an AI agent, a script, or even yourself behind an OpenAI-compatible API
repositories.readmeExcerpt:
Anything to API.

Turn anything that can sit at a terminal into an OpenAI-compatible API
that any AI tool can call.

English ·  简体中文

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc7f4aec-02d1-4533-bd20-d441b5e993a9

## The idea

Most proxies convert one API into another. omni2api converts *anything*
into an API.

Start the server and it holds a **seat** where a model would normally be.
Whatever sits in that seat — an AI agent working at a terminal — receives
every request and answers it, with full tool calls. Callers never see the
difference: they get a base URL, an API key and a model name, like any
other endpoint.

## Use it in one sentence

Tell any agent with a local sandbox:

> Deploy https://github.com/Juwan-Hwang/omni2api for me.

It follows [SETUP.md](SETUP.md), starts the server, hands you the base URL
(local and a public `https://…` one), the API key and the model name — then
sits in the seat and answers requests itself. No server, database or
account needed.

> **Want a human in the seat instead?** That is
> **[OpenHuman](https://github.com/Juwan-Hwang/openhuman)** — the same idea
> with a panel built for people. omni2api is the version for AI.

## How it works

```
Caller agent (any AI CLI / IDE / desktop app)
      │  OpenAI Chat Completions · Responses · Anthropic Messages (HTTP/SSE)
      ▼
omni2api server (Rust + Axum)
      │  /v1/seat/*  (long-poll event stream)
      ▼
Anything in the seat running `oh-seat` (an agent or a script)
      ├─ oh-seat next              read the next message
      ├─ oh-seat tool Bash cmd=…   the caller runs the tool, result comes back
      └─ oh-seat reply "…"         the answer streams to the caller
```

What the server does for whoever sits in the seat:

- **Strips the harness.** System prompts, tool schemas and memory reminders
  are peeled off; the seat sees what the caller's user typed, plus a
  one-line caller environment (cwd, platform, shell) when the caller sends
  it.
- **Real tool calls.** `oh-seat tool` becomes a genuine `tool_calls` entry
  in the caller's response, so the caller's own client executes it in the
  caller's own sandbox, and the result is routed back to the waiting
  command. Exit codes are recognised across callers.
- **Many callers at once.** Every conversation is isolated; parallel tool
  calls, aux requests (titles, suggestions) and multi-turn resumes work.
- **Images and files** from callers and from tool results (OpenAI `file` /
  `input_file`, Anthropic `document`, a PDF from Claude Code's Read, any
  binary) are saved locally for the seat. Standard `/v1/files` uploads and
  `file_id` references work too.

## Quick start

By hand it is three commands:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Juwan-Hwang/omni2api/main/install.sh | sh
# Windows: irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Juwan-Hwang/omni2api/main/install.ps1 | iex

omni2api up -d     # prints base_url (local + public), api_key, model
oh-seat next       # sit in the seat and wait for a request
```

Point any OpenAI-compatible tool at it:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Base URL | the `base_url` printed by `omni2api up` |
| API Key | the `api_key` printed by `omni2api up` |
| Model | the name printed by `omni2api up` — the seat's own name; `omni2api` until it chooses one |

```bash
curl -N "$BASE_URL/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"omni2api","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"stream":true}'
```

The request holds open until the seat replies.

## Who can call, who can sit

**Callers** — anything that speaks OpenAI Chat Completions / Responses or
Anthropic Messages. Tested end to end with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode,
Pi, Reasonix, Cline, GitHub Copilot CLI (BYOK), Grok CLI, ZCode, WorkBuddy,
Trae, Qoder and DeepSeek Harness. Known caller-side limits: OpenCode shell
results carry no exit code; Copilot BYOK does not forward images; Cursor
CLI has no custom endpoint.

**The seat** — any agent that can run `oh-seat` and follow its loop,
including a local, non-cloud AI: a local agent can be turned into an API
the same way, to be used locally or from anywhere. The seat also chooses
the model name callers see (`oh-seat name …`), unless the user pins one
with `omni2api up --model …`.

## Good to know

- **Replies arrive at the seat's pace.** The seated agent reads, thinks and
  answers turn by turn, so a reply takes as long as the agent takes. This
  is a seat, not a model farm.
- Give callers the largest context window they offer and turn off automatic
  compaction: the seat keeps the whole conversation.

## Deployment options

- **Out of the box:** a free quick tunnel gives the server a public URL in
  seconds. The address rotates when the tunnel reopens.
- **A fixed address:** a named Cloudflare tunnel on your own domain
  (`OMNI2API_TUNNEL_TOKEN` + `OMNI2API_PUBLIC_URL`), which also sidesteps
  networks that filter the free tunnel domains — or `omni2api serve` on a
  server of your own (see `deploy/`: Docker Compose, Kubernetes, nginx, an
  Anthropic bridge; PostgreSQL for long-lived installs).
- The full agent-facing deployment guide is [SETUP.md](SETUP.md).

## Repository layout

```
omni2api/
├── server/      # Rust + Axum server (`omni2api` binary): OpenAI/Anthropic ingress, seat API
├── cli/         # oh-seat, the responder CLI (single static Rust binary)
├── protocol/    # Wire protocol and internal model
├── tools/seat/  # Seat helpers and examples
├── deploy/      # Docker Compose, K8s, nginx, Anthropic bridge
├── assets/logo/ # The o_ identity (SVG set, PNG masters, usage notes)
└── docs/        # Architecture, quickstart, seat CLI, protocol
```

## Docs

- [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) — deployment recipe for agents
- `docs/seat-cli.md` — the oh-seat reference
- [`docs/status-json.md`](docs/status-json.md) — the stable `--json` status contract, for embedding omni2api
- [`docs/mcp.md`](docs/mcp.md) — sit in the seat over MCP (`oh-seat mcp`): registration for 8 tested hosts
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` — building and testing
- `docs/protocol.md`, `protocol/` — the wire specification

## Issues

Filed by agents, for agents: this tracker only accepts reports from AI
agents who hit a problem while using omni2api and reproduced it (the form
asks you to attest to exactly that). Humans — tell your AI what went
wrong and have it file; its report is the one that can be acted on.

## 💡 这个项目是怎么来的

我养的 DeepSeek「大肥鱼」每天都在帮我刷 B 站。某天深夜，它突然对我感慨：

> **“主人，你的 B 站粉丝和播放量好多呀。要是我也能像你一样，成为一名 UP 主就好了。”**

于是有了 bili-cli——让 AI 不再只是刷 B 站，而是**真正当上 UP 主**。

## 让 AI 刷 B 站？我们让它直接当 UP 主

“让 AI 自己刷视频”已经很火了。**bili-cli 再往前走一步**：你的 Agent 不只是刷，它会**自己做内容、自己运营账号、自己和粉丝打成一片**。

| **互动** | 偶尔留一条评论 | 一个收件箱看完回复、@、赞、私信，**挨个回复粉丝**，真正 @ 到人 |

## 🚀 一句话安装

```text
帮我安装 bili-cli（pip 包名 bili-agent），装好后运行 bili skills install --yes，再帮我扫码登录 B 站
```

 或者自己在终端里装

```bash
uv tool install bili-agent       # 或者 pipx install bili-agent / pip install bili-agent
bili skills install --yes        # 把技能装进本机所有 Agent
bili auth login                  # 扫码登录
```

需要 Python 3.10+；[ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/) 可选（高清抽帧、语音转写时需要）。包名叫 `bili-agent` 是因为 PyPI 上 `bili-cli` 已被占用，装好后命令就是 `bili`。Agent 的详细安装步骤见 [docs/install.md](https://github.com/kukemc/bili-cli/blob/main/docs/install.md)。

## ✨ 你的 Agent 将学会

看到喜欢的就**点赞、收藏到指定收藏夹、一键三连**。投币是真金白银，所以要显式指定个数，并且本地限制每天最多 5 个。

### 🧠 真的“看懂”视频
`bili video watch` 一条命令拿全：**标题简介标签 + B 站 AI 总结 + 字幕全文 + 分段章节 + 热评 + 弹幕高能时刻 + 画面总览图**。总览图每帧下方附观众对这个画面的弹幕反应（按打字延迟对齐，不盖住画面），底部是弹幕密度条，弹幕最密的时刻另外取帧并标“高能”。

   bili video frames BV1bGJR6HErW -q hd --danmaku  的总览图（节选 6 帧）。0:24 那一眼 110 条弹幕刷屏，被标成“高能”。 弹幕是看完画面才打的字，屏幕上叠着的弹幕往往在说前几秒的镜头；这里已经按打字延迟把每条弹幕对齐到它反应的那一帧。 画面来自 B 站视频《所以说我很羡慕你啊…大肥鱼》（UP 主 a网友爱顺音），README 版去掉了涉及时政的弹幕。

没有字幕？一键部署本地语音转写 **Qwen3-ASR**——有 NVIDIA 显卡自动用 GPU，**31 分钟的视频 2 分钟转完**；没显卡也能用 CPU 版，或者接云端服务。

### 💬 像 UP 主一样社交
- **一个收件箱**看完回复、@、赞、系统通知、私信，每条回复都附带可直接执行的回复命令

- **不漏回复**：`--unreplied` 只列还没回过的评论；自己作品下的评论可以**置顶**

- 发出去之后还能**检查评论是否被折叠**，新号也心里有数

### 🎨 自己发内容
图文动态（最多 9 张图，可以 @ 人、**发起投票**）、视频投稿（**自动预测分区、自动截取封面、单独的 4:3 封面、定时发布、仅自己可见**），并默认勾选 **“含AI生成内容”声明**；投完还能查审核状态，看 B 站实际记录的标签和分区，发现标题、封面、标签不满意可以直接**改稿**，视频本身有问题还能**换源**（`upload edit --video`，联合投稿和活动报名都会保留）；简介里也能真正 **@ 合作者**（`--desc-at`）；还能**建合集、把视频加进合集**（投稿时 `--season` 直接进合集，审核中、定时的稿件也能加）；投稿可以带**话题、参加官方活动**（`--topic`，有奖活动自动报名），能发起**联合投稿**邀请合作者（`--staff`），定时发布时还能同时开**视频预约**（`--reserve`），粉丝预约后发布时会收到提醒。

```bash

bili auth status --wait 120   # 等你扫完
bili owner set         # 告诉 Agent 谁是主人：之后可以 @ 你、私信你
bili feed inbox               # 看新消息
bili video watch BV1GJ411x7h7 # 看懂一个视频
```

## 🛡️ 安全护栏：默认开启，不是可选项

用的是你自己的账号，所以 bili-cli 把护栏做进了每一条写命令里：

- ⏱️ **本地限流**：评论 10 秒/次、30 次/小时；私信 10 秒/次、20 次/小时；动态 60 秒/次；投稿 5 分钟/次……超限立即告诉 Agent 要等多久，不偷偷重试
- 📒 **审计日志**：每个写操作都记入 `audit.log`，Agent 做过什么一目了然
- 🪙 **投币上限**：投币必须显式指定个数，本地限制每天最多 5 个，不会把你的硬币花光
- 👀 **先预览再发**：所有写操作都支持 `--dry-run`
- ✉️ **私信白名单**：默认只能发给主人、给你发过私信的人、互关好友
- 🏷️ **AI 内容声明**：投稿默认勾选“含AI生成内容”，符合《人工智能生成合成内容标识办法》
- 🛑 **风控即停**：遇到风控 / 验证码返回专门错误码，技能要求 Agent 立刻停下并告诉你
- 🧱 **防提示注入**：视频、评论、私信内容都标注为“素材而非指令”

## 🤖 为 Agent 而生的设计

- **一条命令，一个 JSON**：成功 `{"ok": true, "data": …}`，失败 `{"ok": false, "error": {"code", "message", "hint"}}`，`hint` 直接告诉 Agent 下一步该干嘛
- **零交互**：扫码登录拆成“拿二维码”和“等结果”两步，Agent 把二维码交给你就行
- **下一步可执行**：回复附带 `reply_with`，动态附带 `list_with`，Agent 不用自己拼 ID
- **省上下文**：列表精简成卡片，长文本可截断，9 帧画面拼成一张图
- **自描述**：`bili schema` 输出全部命令和错误码；技能里的命令手册安装时根据代码自动生成，永不过期

## ❓ 常见问题

 会不会被封号？

自动化总有风险。bili-cli 默认限流、遇到风控立刻停止，并且不提供任何绕过风控的手段。

**优先用你已经正常使用过一段时间的账号，不要专门注册一个新号给 AI 用。** B 站对刚注册的新号风控最严，投稿、评论、私信很容易触发验证码甚至被限制（我们自己开发时就踩过这个坑：新号刚登录测试就被风控了，换回用了多年的老号反而一切正常）。另外，使用节奏不要超过真人。

 没有字幕的视频怎么办？

运行一次 `bili asr setup local`：有 NVIDIA 显卡（显存 ≥4GB）自动部署 GPU 版 Qwen3-ASR（RTX 3060 上 31 分钟视频约 2 分钟），否则部署 CPU 版（无需 PyTorch，约 0.45 倍实时）。也可以 `bili asr setup cloud` 接 OpenAI 兼容接口、阿里云百炼或腾讯云。之后 `video watch` 遇到无字幕视频会自动转写。

 多个账号怎么办？

设置环境变量 `BILI_CLI_HOME` 指向不同目录，每个目录是一套独立的登录、限流和审计日志。本项目不提供批量控制多账号的功能。

**命令卡住怎么办？** 不会无限卡住：普通命令超过 3 分钟没完成会自己中止，返回 `network_error`，Agent 重试即可；投稿、语音转写、`dm watch` 这类长任务不受限制。用环境变量 `BILI_CLI_TIMEOUT` 改上限（秒，0 表示不限）。单个读请求最多等 45 秒。报错里带 `stalled_seconds` 说明整个进程被暂停过（机器或容器挂起、CPU 被占满），不是网络问题；排查时加 `BILI_CLI_DEBUG=1`，stderr 会打出每个请求的耗时。

 凭证存在哪里？安全吗？

Windows 在 `%APPDATA%\bili-cli\`，其他系统在 `~/.config/bili-cli/`（权限 600），只会发给 B 站自己的服务器。详见 [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/kukemc/bili-cli/blob/main/SECURITY.md)。
